clue.text: Setter to lay down the law about missing muse

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as me

indicators.note: missing tells us the word for about is dropped from the longer word

parts.note: to dictate is to give orders with authority
C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A crossword setter, laying down the law, finds inspiration has deserted him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' is the crossword compiler speaking of himself; 'missing' drops C (circa, about) from the law-laying verb, leaving DITATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To muse is to ponder quietly, a synonym of contemplate or reflect deeply.

clue.text: Fool shows hesitation over prince's favourite

indicators.note: in a down clue, over signals the hesitation word is turned upward

parts.note: um is a sound of hesitation
P is an abbreviation for prince
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: A jester stammers in front of the prince's darling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns UM into MU.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British slang for a silly or incompetent person, an idiot.

clue.text: Up to a point the German instinct is to sneer

parts.note: der is a German word for the
the id is the instinctive part of the mind in Freud
E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: To some extent, a German's natural urge is to mock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up to a' only joins: the pieces run DER, ID, and finally the compass point E.
explanation.definitionFit: Deride and sneer both mean to mock with contempt, verbs in the infinitive.

clue.text: Kitchen utensil can undo even beers

parts.note: a can is a tin
to undo a fastening is to open it

indicators.note: even picks the letters in even positions of beers, the second and fourth

explanation.surface: A gadget for the kitchen can take the tops off even beers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'even' takes the 2nd and 4th letters of beers, E and R.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand tool found in kitchens for cutting the lids off cans of food.

clue.text: A small number aim to go back for test manoeuvre

parts.note: three is a small number
to aim is to point
to turn is to go back the other way

explanation.surface: A few people aim to return for a driving examination.
explanation.walkthrough: In the UK driving test, candidates must turn the car round in a road using forward and reverse moves.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard turning manoeuvre examined in the British driving test.

clue.text: High Street has done badly

indicators.note: badly signals the following word's letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: The high street has performed poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High Street' reads as a shopping street, but High is the definition. 'badly' rearranges DONE to ONED.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for intoxicated by drugs, so high in the sense of drugged.

clue.text: It is found in bottom half of battle inscription

indicators.note: is found in places the word it inside the other piece
bottom half of a down entry means the last three of the six letters of battle

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something is located in the lower part of a battle's written record.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the 'bottom half' of the six-letter battle is its last three letters; 'is found in' places the pronoun within them.
explanation.definitionFit: A title is a heading or caption, a written or engraved label.

clue.text: Delicacies in hampers from the French Riviera?

parts.note: Nice is a resort city on the French Riviera
hampers as a verb means ties, restrains

explanation.surface: Fancy foods packed in picnic baskets shipped from the south of France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hampers' looks like picnic baskets but is a verb meaning restricts; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Niceties are fine points or subtleties, delicate refinements of manner.

clue.text: Commit 500 European revolutionary separatists to chase detectives around

indicators.note: to chase means come after, so this piece follows the previous ones

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500

indicators.note: around turns the detectives' letters back to front

parts.note: the CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

indicators.note: revolutionary means the separatists' letters are turned round

parts.note: ETA was the Basque separatist group

explanation.surface: Five hundred European rebels are dispatched to pursue police officers.
explanation.walkthrough: ETA was the Basque separatist group in Spain; 'revolutionary' and 'around' each turn their piece backwards, and 'to chase' sets the separatists last.
explanation.definitionFit: To dedicate oneself is to commit or devote oneself to a cause.

clue.text: I enchant drunk with island tale that happened long ago

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: I charm a drunk with a story from an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges I ENCHANT into ANCIENTH.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for events from the distant past, no longer relevant.

clue.text: Standard charge in return for companion

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level

indicators.note: in return reverses the letters of the charge

parts.note: rent is a charge for use of property

explanation.surface: A fixed fee given back in exchange for company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in return' turns RENT into TNER.
explanation.definitionFit: A partner is a companion or associate, a mate.

clue.text: Refusal to overturn it before last month's return is seen

indicators.note: before places the earlier pieces ahead of the month

parts.note: no is a refusal

indicators.note: to overturn means the word it is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: return turns the month's abbreviation back to front

parts.note: Dec, December, is the last month of the year

explanation.surface: A rejection that overturns a tax return filed at year's end is spotted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to overturn' gives TI and 'return' gives CED.
explanation.definitionFit: Noticed and seen both mean observed or spotted, past participles.

clue.text: Eventually find oneself caught in open duplicity

indicators.note: caught in means the letters sit within the words open duplicity

explanation.surface: In the end someone is trapped in obvious deceit.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb meaning to arrive finally in some state or place.

clue.text: Person who fits English mansion with proper traditional Italian casement openings

parts.note: a pile is a large stately house

indicators.note: openings means the first letters of the four words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone fits out an English stately home with authentic Italian windows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fits' looks like installing windows but means seizures. 'openings' takes P, T, I and C.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with epilepsy, a condition causing seizures, is subject to fits.

clue.text: Public notice people by junction following a girl and a cat

indicators.note: following means the earlier pieces come after the girl and the cat

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
the ounce is the snow leopard, a big cat
men are people
a T is a road junction shaped like that letter

explanation.surface: A notice put up by a crossroads about a girl and her cat.
explanation.walkthrough: The ounce, or snow leopard, is a big cat seldom met outside crosswords; 'following' sets the people and junction after the girl and cat.
explanation.definitionFit: An announcement is a public statement or declaration.

clue.text: Kindle engages in measures to remove prejudice

indicators.note: engages in means the kindling word goes within the two measures

parts.note: an en is a printer's measure of width, so two of them
the second en from the plural measures
to kindle a fire is to light it

explanation.surface: Kindle e-reader interacts with tools to fight bias.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kindle' looks like the Amazon e-reader but is the verb to set alight; an en is a printer's measure, half an em.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlighten someone is to free them from ignorance or bias.

clue.text: Foreign weightlifter free to leave at the end of the day

indicators.note: foreign suggests the letters are made strange, rearranged
to leave means the letters of free are removed from the fodder

explanation.surface: An overseas weightlifter is allowed to go when the day is over.
explanation.walkthrough: Take F, R, E, E out of WEIGHTLIFTER and rearrange the rest, WIGHTLIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Twilight is dusk, the dim light as day ends at evening.

clue.text: Stops boys surrounding film maker

indicators.note: surrounding means the boys go round the film maker

parts.note: sons are boys
Jacques Tati was a French film director

explanation.surface: Boys crowd round a director to halt him.
explanation.walkthrough: Jacques Tati, maker of Monsieur Hulot's Holiday, is a crossword favourite for film maker; 'Stops' is a noun, places where trains halt.
explanation.definitionFit: Stations are stopping places on a railway or bus route.

clue.text: A hotel we ring turns out to be a pub

indicators.note: turns out suggests the letters are turned into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A hotel we telephone proves to be just a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns out' rearranges A HOTEL WE RING.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British term for a pub, from a place where animals drink.

clue.text: Tell off vehicle parking on far side of street

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
P is the symbol for parking

indicators.note: far side of means the closing letters of street

explanation.surface: A car is parked across the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'far side of' takes ET, the last two letters of street.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is British slang for to reprimand, as if called onto the boss's carpet.

clue.text: Film about shy doctor of medicine

indicators.note: about means the film wraps round the altered letters

parts.note: a pic is a film, short for picture

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered

explanation.surface: A movie about a timid doctor of medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like a physician but is the anagram signal; 'about' puts the result inside the film; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Physic is an archaic word for medicine or a remedy.

clue.text: Takes action as a result of fabrications about central instigators

indicators.note: about means the lies go around the central letters

parts.note: fabrications are lies

indicators.note: central takes the middle five letters of instigators

explanation.surface: Sues because of lies spread about the chief troublemakers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'central' takes the middle five of the eleven letters of instigators; 'about' wraps the fabrications round them; 'as a result of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To litigate is to sue, bringing a legal case to court.

clue.text: Rear of building in French early Renaissance style

indicators.note: rear of takes the closing letter of building

parts.note: en is French for in

indicators.note: early takes the opening letters of Renaissance

explanation.surface: The back of a building done in French early-Renaissance style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'early' takes RE from Renaissance.
explanation.definitionFit: A genre is a category or kind, especially of art or literature.

clue.text: Visual representation used in cryptography

indicators.note: used in means the letters are sitting inside the word cryptography

explanation.surface: A diagram appears in codebreaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A graph is a chart or diagram showing data visually.

clue.text: Horse features in German corny joke

indicators.note: features in means the horse sits within the German abbreviation

parts.note: a roan is a horse with a mixed coat

explanation.surface: A horse appears in a German comedian's tired gag.
explanation.walkthrough: A roan is a horse whose coat mixes white hairs with a darker colour; 'features in' sets it within the German abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A groaner is a pun or joke so bad it makes listeners groan.

clue.text: Spineless creature cops out when challenged

indicators.note: when challenged suggests the letters are disturbed into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A cowardly person backs out when confronted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spineless' looks like cowardice, but an octopus is literally an invertebrate. 'when challenged' rearranges COPS OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: An octopus is an invertebrate, an animal with no backbone.

clue.text: International party leader put on trial

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match
Ed Davey leads the Liberal Democrats, and Ed Miliband led Labour

explanation.surface: An international political leader faces prosecution.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test match is an international game of cricket or rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: Tested means tried out or examined, as when something is given a trial.

clue.text: Heard fruit tonic mixture is sleep-inducing

indicators.note: heard means the fruit's word is spoken, giving a sound-alike spelling

parts.note: a hip is the fruit of the rose

indicators.note: mixture tells us the letters of tonic are mixed up

explanation.surface: A fruit tonic blend is said to make you drowsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heard' turns HIP into HYP; 'mixture' rearranges TONIC into NOTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypnotic describes something that induces sleep or a trance.
